Petitioner in Kum.Mohitha.R., Mvc 744/2022: D/o.Raghavendra, Scch-9 2 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 Aged about 14 years, R/at No.455, Iii Stage, Kalpavrikshanagar, Kesare, Narasimharaja Mohalla, Mysore - 570007. Petitioner in Kum.R.Nethravathi, MVC 745/2022: D/o.Raghavendra, Aged about 11 years, R/at No.455, III Stage, Kalpavrikshanagar, Kesare, Narasimharaja Mohalla, Mysore - 570007. Respondents in all 1) The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., the cases: Regional Office No.44/45, Leo Shopping Complex, Residency Road, Bengaluru - 25. Policy No.215700/31/ SCCH-9 3 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 2021/MI/249608 Valid from 18.03.2021 to 17.03.2022 (By Sri. R.S.Srikanta Reddy -Adv.) 2. Insured Name Shivu.H.N., S/o.Neelegowda, No.385, T.Hoshalli, Belagola Hobli, Srirangapatna Taluk, Mandya District - 571438. (Owner of the Maruti Swift Car, bearing Reg.No.KA-11-N-1518). (Exparte) // COMMON JUDGMENT // These petitions are filed by the petitioners against the Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 2 respondents claiming compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act for the injuries sustained by them in RTA. 2.
texts.facts: The petitioners have violated the provisions of Motor vehicles Act by triple riding. The driver of the offending Car was not holding valid RC and DL on the date of alleged accident. Due to impact of said accident the petitioners have sustained injuries. The accident was caused sole negligence of Car driver and petitioners have sustained injuries.
texts.arguments: Therefore, in view of non production of disability certificate and doctor evidence regarding disability, it cannot be considered as the petitioner is having physical disability due to the accidental injury. There is no physical disability to the petitioner to the accidental injury. Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained, treatment taken and medical bills produced by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award the Global Compensation. The learned counsel for respondent argued that even if SCCH-9 24 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 minors were riding as pillion riders with triple riding that amounts to violation of Motor Vehicle Act and attract contributory negligence. In this regard he has relied upon the following reported judgments: 1) 2004 (1) KLJ 498 (P.S.Somaiah & anr V/s The Director, Bangalore Dairy and Others), wherein it Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 18 is observed that - If any rider of Motor cycle violates Sec.128 of M.V.Act moving in a triple riding then contributory negligence to be considered and compensation should be apportioned on the apportionment of negligence. 2) 2003 (2) TAC 103 (Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Coimbatore Dvn) Ltd., Coimbatore V/s Abdul Salam & Others), wherein Hon'ble Madras High Court observed that riding the motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a negligence and contributory negligence be considered while awarding the compensation in accident case. 3) 2017 ACJ 418 (New India Assurance Co.., Ltd., V/s Hemanth & Others), wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that- in case of triple riding there is a contributory negligence and SCCH-9 25 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 liability to be fixed on apportionment to the insurance companies. 4) The unreported judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.5314/2009 (MV) between H.B. Hemakeshwarappa V/s Abdul Roop Khan
